ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Robert Peary Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing primary care for four months of fatigue, breathlessness, pallor, a sore tongue, and numbness and unsteadiness in the feet: blood tests, neurological and foot examination, falls, mood, the first vitamin B12 injection and a hematology consultation. Concerns: Tired and breathless doing what used to be easy; Numb, unsteady feet on top of feet that lost their toes long ago; He wants to know whether this illness can be treated, and to keep walking and working. [S]

list.item: Fatigue, breathlessness on exertion, pallor with a lemon-yellow tinge, a sore tongue, and numbness and unsteadiness in the feet over about four months, with a macrocytic anemia, low white cells and platelets, a low vitamin B12 and a high methylmalonic acid; cause under evaluation with a hematology consultation: resolved, confirmed [S]

Pernicious anemia (autoimmune gastritis with intrinsic factor antibodies), with severe vitamin B12 deficiency; synthetic modern diagnosis linked to the documented cause of his death: active, confirmed [S]

Subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord with peripheral neuropathy from vitamin B12 deficiency: loss of vibration and joint position sense in the feet, absent ankle jerks, brisk knee jerks and a positive Romberg test: active, confirmed [S]
Absence of the second to fifth toes of the right foot after frostbite and amputation in early middle age; healed stumps; callus under the first metatarsal head: active, confirmed [S]
Absence of the second to fifth toes of the left foot after frostbite and amputation in early middle age; healed stumps: active, confirmed [S]
One fall in a dark bedroom a month ago without injury; unsteady in the dark and on uneven ground; uses a stick outdoors: active, confirmed [S]

Autoimmune atrophic gastritis, corpus-predominant, with intestinal metaplasia and enterochromaffin-like cell hyperplasia in the body of the stomach, a spared antrum, no Helicobacter pylori, no neuroendocrine tumor and no dysplasia: active, confirmed [S]

Iron deficiency without anemia, unmasked by the recovery of red cell production and the poor iron absorption of atrophic gastritis; colonoscopy and endoscopy without a bleeding source: active, confirmed [S]
Blister on the end of the left forefoot over the old amputation stump, from boots not yet broken in, in a foot with reduced sensation; no infection; healed in two weeks: resolved, confirmed [S]

tr.td: Establishing primary care for four months of fatigue, breathlessness, pallor, a sore tongue, and numbness and unsteadiness in the feet: blood tests, neurological and foot examination, falls, mood, the first vitamin B12 injection and a hematology consultation
Eight-day review with the reticulocyte response and potassium, seen the same day by hematology: the cause, the injection plan, endoscopy, autoimmune screening and the nerves
Five-week review on the day of upper endoscopy and colonoscopy: blood count, nerves, falls and feet
Eight-week review: blood count, methylmalonic acid, iron studies, the endoscopy biopsies and surveillance
Fifteen-week review: neurological recovery, iron, lifelong maintenance and the plan ahead
Same-day sick visit for a blister on the left forefoot

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

tr.td: Diagnosis: blood count with MCV, smear and reticulocytes; vitamin B12, methylmalonic acid, homocysteine and folate; iron studies, LDH and bilirubin; kidney function; TSH and HbA1c; all drawn before the first injection
Hematology consultation to confirm the cause and advise on treatment, endoscopy and follow-up

Treatment started at intake without waiting for the cause, because of neurological signs: cyanocobalamin 1,000 micrograms into the muscle every other day for seven doses; no folic acid alone; no transfusion while he is stable at rest

Maintenance: weekly injections, taught for self-injection, until neurological improvement levels off, then monthly injections for life; high-dose oral cyanocobalamin (at least 1 mg a day) offered as an alternative; vitamin B12 levels not rechecked routinely once treated

Response and safety checks: reticulocytes and potassium in the first week, blood count at about five and eight weeks, methylmalonic acid and homocysteine and iron studies at eight weeks, and symptoms at every visit

Stomach: upper endoscopy with biopsies by the updated Sydney protocol to confirm autoimmune gastritis and look for neuroendocrine tumors and dysplasia, with a screening colonoscopy at the same session; surveillance interval set from the findings by shared decision; thyroid antibodies checked

Nerves and falls: neurological examination (vibration, joint position, reflexes, Romberg, gait, cognition) at each visit; physical therapy for balance and gait; night lights and a clear path at home; a stick outdoors and care on ice

Feet: daily skin checks with a mirror, extra-depth shoes with toe fillers and a forefoot rocker sole, no new boots without a fitting, nail and callus care by podiatry every three months, and same-day care for any blister, redness or wound
Mood and cognition: PHQ-9 and MoCA at intake and after treatment, since vitamin B12 deficiency can affect both
Find the cause of the anemia and the numb feet
Pernicious anemia confirmed: intrinsic factor and parietal cell antibodies positive, gastrin high
Normal hemoglobin and MCV within eight weeks
Hemoglobin 8.2 to 14.1 g/dL and MCV 118 to 91 fL at eight weeks
Recover feeling and balance in the feet and walk without falls
At fifteen weeks: vibration sense back at the ankles, Romberg negative, Timed Up and Go 10 seconds, no falls; numbness at the ends of the feet persists
No foot wound that goes unnoticed
Daily foot checks; one blister found early and healed in two weeks; podiatry every three months
Endoscopy without neuroendocrine tumor or dysplasia; repeat in three years by shared decision
